title: Telemetry Chirps & Backpressure Hypotheses — Observability Scrub
content:
Summary:

This is a scratchpad from a short on-call investigation into a new pattern we've been seeing in production telemetry: very brief, repetitive metric blips on exporter ingestion (we're calling them 'chirps') that correlate with transient downstream backpressure and subsequent SLO burn spikes on low-latency paths. The pattern is noisy but reproducible across two regions.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture observations from the pager, immediate triage steps taken, and hypotheses to validate.
- Collect short-term mitigations and longer-term instrumentation changes.
- Provide a clear handoff for engineering teams to pick up experiments.

What we observed (timeline):
- 2025-11-03 02:14 UTC: On-call page for high p99 latency on embed-generation-route in us-west-2.
- 02:15 UTC: Dashboards show repeated ~2s spikes in exporter.ingest.latency (duration metric) every ~30s for 8–12 iterations, labeled as 'chirps'.
- 02:16 UTC: Concurrent increase in exporter.queue.depth by ~40% but no long sustained queue growth.
- 02:17 UTC: Some nodes showing TCP retransmits increases to pods handling Kafka consumer offsets.
- 02:20 UTC: Traffic drop on one canary but overall traffic rerouted by LB; burst of SLO burn tracked to a small percentage of requests hitting older model variant.
- 02:30 UTC: Temporary mitigation (scale up exporter pod count by 20% and increase consumer parallelism) reduced visible chirps but did not eliminate them.

Key dashboards / queries referenced:
- Exporter ingestion dashboard (metrics: exporter.ingest.latency, exporter.batch.size, exporter.queue.depth)
- Kafka consumer lag dashboard (consumer.lag, consumer.retries)
- Network telemetry: tcp.retransmits per node, interface drops
- SLO burnboard for low-latency routes (10ms/50ms buckets)
- Logs: exporter stdout + consumer sidecar logs (grep for "backpressure" and "max_wait_ms")

Immediate triage steps (what we did):
- Correlated exporter chirps with network retransmit spikes using node telemetry (prometheus node exporter + VPC flow logs).
- Restarted the exporter pod on the most affected host to reset TCP connections — temporarily cleared chirps for ~6mins.
- Increased exporter replica count and Kafka consumer concurrency to absorb bursts.
- Deployed a temporary sampling rule in the collector to keep only 10% of high-cardinality debug traces to reduce load on collector pipeline.
- Notified platform networking team and opened OBS-319.

Hypotheses (ranked, with tests):
1) Short-lived TCP-level backpressure between exporter and Kafka broker causes consumer to retry and batch timing to jitter, producing the chirp pattern.
   - Test: Reproduce by throttling egress bandwidth from exporter pods in staging (tc/netem) and observe exporter.ingest.latency pattern.
   - Evidence: TCP retransmits rise right before chirps; restarts temporarily fix it.

2) Collector batching heuristic (max_wait_ms) interacts poorly with intermittent small-retry windows: small retries cause incomplete batches to be flushed more often, leading to latency spikes and queue depth oscillation.
   - Test: Toggle max_wait_ms -> lower value in staging and run load test that simulates intermittent retries.
   - Evidence: Batch size is inversely proportional to chirp amplitude in sampled traces.

3) A small percentage of traffic hitting older model variant (different runtime path) is more sensitive to transient backpressure and creates localized SLO burn while autoscaling is slow to react.
   - Test: Force 100% traffic to current model variant for a short window during a controlled test and observe SLO burn.
   - Evidence: Canary logs show additional timeout retries for older variant.

4) Intermittent node-level NIC interrupts or noisy neighbor causing short stalls for some exporter pods.
   - Test: Check kernel dmesg, irqbalance logs, and correlate with cloud provider metrics. Run node-level stress tests in staging.
   - Evidence: No clear kernel OOM or throttling seen in pod metrics, but host tcp retransmit spikes correlate.

Short-term mitigations (playbook entries we used / suggest):
- If chirps observed: scale exporter replicas by +20% and increase consumer parallelism (give priority to stability over cost during incident).
- Rolling restart targeted exporter pods on affected hosts if tcp retransmits > 50/minute and chirp pattern repeats 3 times within 10 minutes.
- Temporarily increase circuit-breaker timeouts for the older model variant and disable automatic traffic shifting for that variant until root cause identified.
- Add a sampling rule in collector to reduce the volume of high-cardinality debug payloads during surges.

Instrumentation & logging changes (follow-ups):
- Add an exporter-side histogram for inter-batch spacing (time between flushes) and label with consumer instance id so we can see correlation with consumer retries.
- Emit TCP connection metrics from the exporter sidecar (existing sidecar already exposes socket stats but not aggregated into exporter dashboard).
- Add explicit trace spans for batch flush decision (why flush now: max_wait vs max_size vs error) to tie batch reason to latency chirps.
- Short-term: increase retention of raw logs for affected windows by 24h so traces can be reconstructed.

Longer-term changes to consider:
- Revisit max_wait_ms heuristic: make it adaptive to measured egress reliability (increase max_wait if retransmit rate high so we build larger batches rather than flushing prematurely).
- Introduce a backpressure-aware batching algorithm that accepts transient retries and smooths flushes across them.
- Improve LB routing to avoid using old variant under small capacity pressure; make canary fallback faster when backlog grows.
- Consider circuit-breakers at exporter->kafka client to surface more deterministic failures instead of retry storms.

Open action items (owners & ETA):
- Jordan Park: add histogram for inter-batch spacing and sidecar TCP aggregation to exporter dashboard. ETA 2025-11-14.
- Avery Chen: run staging netem tests to reproduce chirp pattern and report steps. ETA 2025-11-12.
- Samir Gupta: validate canary traffic routing and put protective config to prevent older variant from receiving traffic during partial network instability. ETA 2025-11-16.
- Platform networking: investigate node tcp retransmit spikes across two affected hosts (OBS-319). ETA initial findings 2025-11-11.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is this purely infra-level (network) or a compound issue with the batching heuristics? Could be both.
- Why do restarts temporarily reduce chirps? Are we temporarily moving pods to cleaner network paths or resetting socket states so retransmits stop?
- Does our autoscaler respond too slowly for short burst patterns (fast chirps but still cause SLO burn)?

Notes to follow-up on after root cause:
- If network root cause confirmed, schedule a change to health-check routing so in-flight batches are drained smoothly during pod/host maintenance windows.
- If batching heuristic root cause confirmed, add adaptive max_wait and include a per-customer knob for aggressive vs conservative batching.

Slack / comms: #oncall, #platform-networking, #observability. I posted a short incident summary in #oncall at 02:45 UTC and linked OBS-319.

Appendix: quick commands used during triage
- kubectl -n telemetry get pods -l app=exporter -o wide (identify affected host)
- kubectl logs exporter-pod -c exporter --since=15m | grep "flush" | tail -n 100
- kubectl exec -it exporter-pod -- ss -tin state established dst <kafka-broker-ip> (check socket stats)
- tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 100ms 10ms distribution normal (staging experiment)

Last note: This doc is intentionally conversational. Keep iterations here — we should generate a clean runbook once the tests converge on a root cause.
